subject: Compilation error with buildDerivs = T and nimStep

messages.author: 129d6b4eedd84194
messages.subject: Compilation error with buildDerivs = T and nimStep
parts:
I've got a model that runs just fine with MCMC but I'd like to try HMC, and I'm getting a compilation error associated with the step() function when I set buildDerivs = TRUE.

The offending line of code in the nimble model is:
date_idx[i, k+1] <- sum(step(det_time[i, k + 1] - date_vec[])) 

In short, sum(step(...)) finds the appropriate index (date_idx) in a vector of dates (date_vec[] = days since 1970-01-01) associated with a continuous datetime (det_time).

Here's the compilation error:
P_3_ttCjsCode_MID_4_nfCode.cpp: In member function 'virtual CppAD::AD<double> date_idx_L19_UID_96::calculate_ADproxyModel(const indexedNodeInfo&) const':
  P_3_ttCjsCode_MID_4_nfCode.cpp:3087:387:
 
error: invalid 'static_cast' from type 'CppAD::AD<double> (*)(CppAD::AD<double>)' to type 'CppAD::AD<int> (*)(CppAD::AD<double>)'
3087 | stoch_ind_set((**ADproxyModel_date_idx), (ARG1_INDEXEDNODEINFO__.info[0]) - 1, (ARG1_INDEXEDNODEINFO__.info[2]) - 1) =
      ((stoch_ind_get((**ADproxyModel_det_time), (ARG1_INDEXEDNODEINFO__.info[0]) - 1, (ARG1_INDEXEDNODEINFO__.info[2]) - 1) -
      ((eigenBlock_oPADproxyModel_date_vec_comma_1to366_cP).block(0, 0, 366, 1)).array())
      .unaryExpr(std::function< CppAD::AD<int>(CppAD::AD<double>) >( static_cast<CppAD::AD<int> (*)(CppAD::AD<double>)>(&nimDerivs_nimStep)))).sum();

There seems to be an issue with type conversion from between integer and double.  I can see that nimStep produces an integer-valued vector (the R version), so I wonder if that's part of the issue.

Any suggestions for how to solve this problem would be much appreciated!  Also, I can provide a reproduceable example if the issue isn't immediately apparent or is rooted deeper in the model.

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Compilation error with buildDerivs = T and nimStep
parts:
In that case it doesn't look like the model is fully amenable to HMC. The derivative of the step function with respect to det_time would not be well defined. 

You could potentially use HMC on other parts of the model and not on det_time.

To make that work, given the compilation error (which we will need to look into), you might need to write a user-defined function to accomplish the sum(step(...)) calculation you want. 

HTH
Perry

messages.subject: Re: Compilation error with buildDerivs = T and nimStep
parts:
I just wanted to follow up, and let you know I was able to compile the model with buildDerivs = TRUE by following your suggestion to write a user-defined function:

sumStep = nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(0), breaks = double(1)){
    ans <- sum(nimStep(x - breaks))
    return(ans)
    returnType(integer(0))
  })

I declared the returnType as integer, which should (I think) prevent derivative tracking.

It's then called in the model as follows:
date_idx[i, k+1] <- sumStep(x = det_time[i, k + 1], breaks = date_vec[])

messages.author: a8ee75ae1cc1b350
messages.subject: Re: Compilation error with buildDerivs = T and nimStep
parts:
Hi Russ and Perry,

I am encountering a similar issue in a distance sampling model I am using that includes both step() and pnorm() functions. I have written wrapper nimbleFunctions to exclude them from derivative tracking but then encounter this error:
"In C++, a model node is being included in derivatives that does not support them.
          To make this a warning, set `nimbleOptions(unsupportedDerivativeHandling='warn')`.
          To skip this error handling entirely (and allow possible malformed code to be used),
          set `nimbleOptions(unsupportedDerivativeHandling='ignore')`."

I am tempted to suppress this error as prompted but I don't understand if this means that the whole model won't be estimated correctly. In the manual: "functions and distributions that are not supported can still be used in a model, as long as no algorithm tries to take derivatives with respect to node(s) that is (are) not supported", and I don't believe I am since, I think, the derivatives are taken on the continuous nodes that are upstream. I am confused as to why this error hasn't already appeared in this thread because it seems like the same underlying issue. My aim is to get the HMC sampler for the "p_eps_sd" hyperparameter in the toy-model code because this mixes very slowly with the default sampler.

I have 3 questions:
1) why does the model compile fine when there is no wrapper for the step() function but does not compile without a wrapper for the pnorm() function even though in the manual, neither is supported for AD?
2) can anyone comment on the validity of the model given that other users seem to have avoided this issue by wrapping unsupported function for AD in nimbleFunctions?
3) how is my situation different from the above / why did this error message not come up in this thread previously?

Best,
Simon

On Friday, March 14, 2025 at 11:25:44 AM UTC-4 Russ Perry wrote:
Thanks Perry.  It helps to understand why it works.  Cheers.

On Friday, March 14, 2025 at 8:20:38 AM UTC-7 Perry de Valpine wrote:
That's good that you got it working for your purposes.

I think the more important reason it works is that you don't have buildDerivs=TRUE for the nimbleFunction, so there is no attempt to generate derivative-tracking code for this nimbleFunction.


On Thu, Mar 13, 2025 at 10:00 PM RussP <russp...@gmail.com> wrote:
I just wanted to follow up, and let you know I was able to compile the model with buildDerivs = TRUE by following your suggestion to write a user-defined function:

sumStep = nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(0), breaks = double(1)){
    ans <- sum(nimStep(x - breaks))
    return(ans)
    returnType(integer(0))
  })

I declared the returnType as integer, which should (I think) prevent derivative tracking.

It's then called in the model as follows:
date_idx[i, k+1] <- sumStep(x = det_time[i, k + 1], breaks = date_vec[])


On Thursday, March 13, 2025 at 4:19:48 PM UTC-7 Perry de Valpine wrote:
In that case it doesn't look like the model is fully amenable to HMC. The derivative of the step function with respect to det_time would not be well defined. 

You could potentially use HMC on other parts of the model and not on det_time.

To make that work, given the compilation error (which we will need to look into), you might need to write a user-defined function to accomplish the sum(step(...)) calculation you want. 

HTH
Perry


On Thu, Mar 13, 2025 at 3:55 PM 'Russ Perry' via nimble-users <nimble...@googlegroups.com> wrote:
date_vec is defined in constants, but det_time is sampled in the MCMC.  This is for a time-varying covariate CJS model model where the detection time (det_time) is sometimes latent for unobserved individuals.  So det_time is sampled given the distribution of observed times of detected individuals in order to integrate over unobserved time-varying covariates. It's a bit more complicated, but that's the gist.

On Thursday, March 13, 2025 at 3:41:22 PM UTC-7 Perry de Valpine wrote:
Are det_time and/or date_vec constants? Or are they model nodes that will be sampled during MCMC? 

On Thu, Mar 13, 2025 at 3:21 PM 'Russ Perry' via nimble-users <nimble...@googlegroups.com> wrote:
I've got a model that runs just fine with MCMC but I'd like to try HMC, and I'm getting a compilation error associated with the step() function when I set buildDerivs = TRUE.

The offending line of code in the nimble model is:
date_idx[i, k+1] <- sum(step(det_time[i, k + 1] - date_vec[])) 

In short, sum(step(...)) finds the appropriate index (date_idx) in a vector of dates (date_vec[] = days since 1970-01-01) associated with a continuous datetime (det_time).

Here's the compilation error:
P_3_ttCjsCode_MID_4_nfCode.cpp: In member function 'virtual CppAD::AD<double> date_idx_L19_UID_96::calculate_ADproxyModel(const indexedNodeInfo&) const':
  P_3_ttCjsCode_MID_4_nfCode.cpp:3087:387:
 
error: invalid 'static_cast' from type 'CppAD::AD<double> (*)(CppAD::AD<double>)' to type 'CppAD::AD<int> (*)(CppAD::AD<double>)'
3087 | stoch_ind_set((**ADproxyModel_date_idx), (ARG1_INDEXEDNODEINFO__.info[0]) - 1, (ARG1_INDEXEDNODEINFO__.info[2]) - 1) =
      ((stoch_ind_get((**ADproxyModel_det_time), (ARG1_INDEXEDNODEINFO__.info[0]) - 1, (ARG1_INDEXEDNODEINFO__.info[2]) - 1) -
      ((eigenBlock_oPADproxyModel_date_vec_comma_1to366_cP).block(0, 0, 366, 1)).array())
      .unaryExpr(std::function< CppAD::AD<int>(CppAD::AD<double>) >( static_cast<CppAD::AD<int> (*)(CppAD::AD<double>)>(&nimDerivs_nimStep)))).sum();

There seems to be an issue with type conversion from between integer and double.  I can see that nimStep produces an integer-valued vector (the R version), so I wonder if that's part of the issue.

Any suggestions for how to solve this problem would be much appreciated!  Also, I can provide a reproduceable example if the issue isn't immediately apparent or is rooted deeper in the model.

Thanks!

--

messages.subject: Re: Compilation error with buildDerivs = T and nimStep
parts:
Hi Simon,
Apologies your question sat for a while. For context, since models and algorithms are separate, the warning given when compiling the model is the best that can be done (i.e. it can't actually error-trap based on an algorithm because it doesn't know how an algorithm will use the model). If your algorithm (an HMC in your case) were attempting to get derivatives for some model calculation that lacks derivative support, you would (should) get an error either when the algorithm is configured (ideally, if the error trapping does its job) or (worse) when it runs. You asked why this warning hadn't appeared in Russ' previous question on this thread. I would guess that's because he encountered a compilation error prior to when the warning would be issued. I'd think subsequently, he would have seen this warning, but perhaps didn't report it as it wasn't the topic of a question. He can confirm (if still following this).
To your other questions:
1. I think nimStep is actually supported (and may have mis-stated above), with 0 derivative everywhere (and I don't think well defined right at 0), so will have to check the manual and whether this makes sense. I think pnorm is not supported. I think the reason Russ encountered an issue with nimStep support involving using it in the larger expression in his code.
2. I'm hoping this is implicitly addressed.
3. I think I addressed this above.
HTH. Thanks for bringing the confusion to our attention.
Perry
